idiom_name: null / Option.empty / akka.NotUsed / empty anonymous implementation
implementation_notes: Scala runs on the JVM, so null still compiles into any reference parameter, but idiomatic code models absence with Option (None) and library code that needs a materialised but uninteresting value takes a sentinel instead: Akka's NotUsed is the ecosystem's canonical placeholder type, documented as used in generic type signatures wherever the actual value is of no importance, a combination of Scala's Unit and Java's Void. Where a concrete interface is demanded, an anonymous empty implementation (new Collaborator { def log(e: String): Unit = () }) or a mock from ScalaMock/Mockito supplies a placeholder; those mocks are strict or default-answering depending on configuration, which makes them stubs rather than inert dummies.
pitfalls: null in Scala is a deliberate escape hatch: under -Yexplicit-nulls (Scala 3) it stops compiling, so a dummy has to become Option.empty or a sentinel in projects that enable it - and those projects are the ones most likely to care about the distinction.

An empty anonymous implementation must implement every abstract member, so a member added to the trait later breaks the test at compile time (good); extending a trait that provides defaults hides the new member instead (bad).

ScalaMock/Mockito mocks used as placeholders fail on unexpected calls or answer defaults depending on configuration: a strict mock turns the dummy into a false alarm, a lenient one hides that the parameter became used.
